entity_title: PPSN (Personal Public Service Number) — application and emergency tax
fact_text: A PPSN is the unique identifier you need to access employment, tax, social welfare, public services and government information in Ireland; anyone taking up work needs one.
evidence_quote: A Personal Public Service (PPS) Number helps you access social welfare benefits, public services and information in Ireland.

entity_title: PPSN (Personal Public Service Number) — application and emergency tax
fact_text: You apply for a PPSN online at MyWelfare (mywelfare.ie); the online service is for people living in Ireland who are 18 or over.
evidence_quote: This service is available at mywelfare.ie for people living in Ireland who are 18 or over.

entity_title: PPSN (Personal Public Service Number) — application and emergency tax
fact_text: If you start work before your PPSN and job are registered with Revenue, your employer must tax all your pay at the higher emergency rate of 40% until your tax record is set up.
evidence_quote: Your employer will tax all your pay at the higher rate of tax (40%).

entity_title: PPSN (Personal Public Service Number) — application and emergency tax
fact_text: On top of income tax, an emergency Universal Social Charge (USC) applies as a flat rate (8% in 2026) on all income while you are on the emergency basis.
evidence_quote: The emergency rate of USC is a flat percentage rate (8% in 2026) applied to all income.

entity_title: IRP card — first-time registration timeline and fee
fact_text: Non-EEA nationals (from outside the EU, EEA, UK or Switzerland) who intend to reside in Ireland for more than 90 days must register their immigration permission with Immigration Service Delivery (ISD).
evidence_quote: If you are coming from outside the EU, EEA, UK or Switzerland and intend to reside in Ireland for more than 90 days you must register a permission to remain with Immigration Service Delivery (ISD).

entity_title: IRP card — first-time registration timeline and fee
fact_text: You must register your immigration permission within 90 days of arriving in Ireland.
evidence_quote: You must register your permission within 90 days of arriving in Ireland.

entity_title: IRP card — first-time registration timeline and fee
fact_text: After you register, your IRP card is posted to the address you provide; you should receive it within 10 working days.
evidence_quote: We will post your IRP card to the address you give us. You should receive it within 10 working days.

entity_title: IRP card — first-time registration timeline and fee
fact_text: The first-time registration fee is €300 per person (where applicable) and can be paid by credit or debit card only.
evidence_quote: The registration fee is €300 (per person), if applicable. You can pay this fee by credit or debit card only.

entity_title: Bringing a pet from Spain to Ireland — EU pet travel rules
fact_text: Because Spain is an EU country, you follow the EU pet travel steps to bring your cat, dog or ferret to Ireland.
evidence_quote: If you are coming to Ireland from another EU country you should follow the steps below to bring your cat, dog (including guide dogs) or ferret with you to Ireland.

entity_title: Bringing a pet from Spain to Ireland — EU pet travel rules
fact_text: Your pet must be microchipped BEFORE it is vaccinated against rabies — the order is mandatory and cannot be reversed.
evidence_quote: Your cat, dog or ferret must be microchipped before it is vaccinated against rabies.

entity_title: Bringing a pet from Spain to Ireland — EU pet travel rules
fact_text: A rabies vaccination is required after microchipping; the pet must be at least 12 weeks old when it is vaccinated.
evidence_quote: Your pet must be at least 12 weeks old when it is vaccinated.

entity_title: Bringing a pet from Spain to Ireland — EU pet travel rules
fact_text: You need an EU pet passport (issued by an EU country) to bring the pet into Ireland.
evidence_quote: You need an EU pet passport issued by an EU country or one of the countries listed above, to enter Ireland.

entity_title: Bringing a pet from Spain to Ireland — EU pet travel rules
fact_text: For dogs, a vet must give a tapeworm treatment between 1 and 5 days before you arrive in Ireland, recorded in the pet passport.
evidence_quote: The treatment must be given by a vet between 1 and 5 days before you arrive in Ireland, and recorded in the pet passport.

entity_title: Ireland outside the Schengen area — separate immigration system
fact_text: Ireland is not part of the Schengen Area, so travelling between Ireland and Schengen countries means passing through an immigration checkpoint with your passport or national ID.
evidence_quote: Ireland is not part of the Schengen Area, which means that if you travel to the Schengen Area from Ireland, you pass through an immigration checkpoint and must show your passport or national identity card.

entity_title: Ireland outside the Schengen area — separate immigration system
fact_text: A Schengen visa does not admit you to Ireland — non-EEA nationals may need a separate Irish visa even if they hold a Schengen visa.
evidence_quote: If you are not a citizen of an EEA member state (the EU plus Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein), you may need a visa to travel to Ireland, even if you have a Schengen visa.

entity_title: Ireland outside the Schengen area — separate immigration system
fact_text: An Irish Residence Permit (IRP) does not by itself allow Schengen travel — a non-EEA resident of Ireland may need a separate Schengen visa to visit Schengen countries.
evidence_quote: If you are a non-EEA citizen and you currently live in Ireland, you may need a Schengen visa to travel to the Schengen Area, even if you have a valid Irish Residence Permit (IRP).

entity_title: Dublin rental market — practical realities
fact_text: The private rental market in Ireland is tight and it can be difficult to find accommodation, especially in Dublin.
evidence_quote: It can be difficult to find private rented accommodation.

entity_title: Dublin rental market — practical realities
fact_text: Most rentals are advertised on accommodation websites, where you can search and set up alerts for your requirements.
evidence_quote: Most rooms, flats, apartments and houses to rent are advertised on accommodation websites.

entity_title: Dublin rental market — practical realities
fact_text: Rentals are usually let on a fixed-term tenancy covering a set period, for example 6 months or a year or more.
evidence_quote: A fixed-term tenancy is an agreement that covers a specific amount of time. For example, it can be for 6 months or a year or more.

entity_title: Dublin rental market — practical realities
fact_text: If you sign one lease together with others (a joint tenancy), each tenant is responsible for ALL the rent — you can be liable for the whole amount if a housemate does not pay.
evidence_quote: If you sign a lease together with other people, you each become responsible for all the rent.
